info.title: Canonical API
info.description:
Company search for developers: describe the companies you want in natural language (or with typed filters) and get back verified, structured company profiles.

Authentication

Every request needs an API key in the `x-api-key` header. Create keys in [Settings → API Keys](/settings). Keys start with `sk_`.

Credits

Result-bearing calls consume credits (each endpoint documents its cost); responses carry `credits_used` and `credits_remaining`.

Rate limits

Per-organization, by plan (see the [rate limits guide](/documentation/rate-limits)). A `429` response includes a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

get.description:
Describe the companies you want in plain English; the interpreter extracts structured criteria, the engine retrieves and LLM-verifies candidates, and you get back structured company profiles. Send `Accept: text/event-stream` to stream results as they verify (SSE events: `meta`, `batch`, `partial_batch`, `preview`, `done`); omit it for a single batch JSON response.

**Credits:** 1 credit per strong (verified) result returned. Partial matches (`include_partials=true`) are not billed. The response reports `credits_used` and `credits_remaining`.

**MCP twin:** `search_companies`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Natural-language search query, e.g. `AI healthcare startups in Boston with over 50 employees`.

parameters.name: top_k
parameters.description: Number of results to return (NL mode).

parameters.name: intent
parameters.description: Optional ranking profile applied after relevance filtering. Omit to let the server infer intent from the query; unknown slugs return 422 with the valid set.

parameters.name: include_partials
parameters.description: Also return LLM-evaluated partial matches (close but not strong). Partials are not billed.

parameters.name: exclude_company_domain
parameters.description: Repeat to exclude companies by domain, e.g. `?exclude_company_domain=stripe.com&exclude_company_domain=square.com`. Unresolvable domains appear in the response `warnings`.

post.description:
Same engine as GET, plus **structured mode**: post a JSON body with `description` and/or typed `filters` to skip natural-language interpretation entirely. Provide exactly one of the `q` query parameter or a structured body — both (or neither) returns 422. Structured mode is batch JSON only; requesting `text/event-stream` with a structured body returns 406. **Credits:** 1 credit per strong (verified) result returned. Partial matches (`include_partials=true`) are not billed. The response reports `credits_used` and `credits_remaining`.

**MCP twin:** `search_companies`.

post.description:
Disambiguate free-text company names into canonical domains before chaining into search, similar, or details calls. Per input name you get ranked `candidates` plus an `auto_resolve_recommended` flag: when true, proceed with `primary_candidate_domain`; when false, show the candidates and let your user pick.

**Credits:** 1 per call when at least one name returns a candidate; a no-match call is free.

**MCP twin:** `lookup_companies`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: One or more company names. Repeat the parameter to look up several (max 10 per call; split longer lists across sequential calls). A trailing legal form (GmbH, SE, S.A., Inc…) is handled for you, so don't also send the bare name.

post.description:
Given a seed company (`company_domain` — the `domain` field from search or lookup results), returns companies similar to it. Dual-mode like search: by default you get a single batch JSON response with any `intent` ranking already applied server-side. Send `Accept: text/event-stream` to stream results as they arrive instead (SSE events: `meta`, `batch`, `partial_batch`, `sorted_order`, `done`); in streaming mode a non-default `intent` emits a late `sorted_order` event carrying `ordered_domains` — apply it client-side once ranking finishes.

**Credits:** 1 per strong result.

**MCP twin:** `find_similar_companies`.

200.description: Companies similar to the seed — batch JSON by default, SSE on request.

get.description:
Full detail payload for one company, addressed by domain — the public identifier returned by search, lookup, and similar results. `company` carries the canonical profile (including `defunct`); `people` lists cofounders and C-suite/execs with role, LinkedIn URL, and prior companies (each prior company includes a `domain` you can feed back into this endpoint to walk the graph). `leadership_data` reports coverage: `available`, `not_available` (company known, but not in the leadership subset — most companies), or `error` (transient lookup failure).

When the company has known ownership edges, the payload also carries a `relationships` block (key absent otherwise): `parents` (all direct parents with their `relation`), `ultimate_parent` and `lineage` (ordered root → immediate parent; both null/empty when ownership is ambiguous, e.g. joint ventures — fall back to `parents`), and `children` grouped by relation category (`subsidiary`, `product_of`, `joint_venture`, `merger`, `other`). Child lists are complete — never truncated. Every related company includes a `domain`; feed it back into this endpoint to walk the corporate family. `source` reports the edges' provenance (e.g. `analyst_curated`) and is present when all edges share one origin.

When we hold job-board data for the company, `company.hiring` carries its current openings: `active_job_count` (total open roles), `has_remote_job`, and three ranked breakdowns of `{name, count}` — `by_department` (up to 15), `by_country` (up to 10, country names rather than ISO2 codes) and `by_city` (up to 5). It comes from a weekly scrape of the company's own job board and counts active postings only.

`hiring` is **absent** when we hold no posting data, which is not the same as the company not hiring — coverage is roughly 20,000 companies. Treat a missing block as "no data", never as "no open roles". The breakdowns are ranked top-Ns for display, not complete sets (the largest company in the data posts across 3,371 distinct cities) — to FILTER on hiring, use the `jobs` filters on `POST /api/v1/search`, which match against the full lists.

A subdomain resolves through its **registered domain** when only the parent is a known company: `coilcoatings.akzonobel.com` returns AkzoNobel. The response then carries `requested_domain`, `matched_domain` and `resolved_via: "registered_domain"`, and the profile is the PARENT company's — check `relationships.children` for the specific unit. All three keys are absent when the requested domain resolved exactly.

**Credits:** 1, charged only when the domain resolves to a real company — a 404 is free.

**MCP twin:** `get_company_details`.

get.description:
Credit balance, plan, and search rate limits for the authenticated organization. `credits` breaks the balance into buckets (`total`, `subscription`, `extra`) with `subscription_resets_at` (ISO datetime, or null with no active subscription). Poll it to check remaining credits and pace requests against `rate_limits` before a paid call.

**Free:** this endpoint charges no credits and is not rate-limited — unlike the result-bearing endpoints, so no 402 or 429.

**MCP twin:** `get_account_status`.

LookupResult.description:
Candidates for one input name plus a disambiguation recommendation.

When `auto_resolve_recommended` is true the match is unambiguous — proceed
with `primary_candidate_domain`. When false, present `candidates` to the
user and let them pick before chaining into another endpoint.
LookupResult.title: LookupResult

intent.description: Optional ranking-profile slug applied after relevance filtering (e.g. 'sales_timing'). Omit for relevance-only ordering. Same taxonomy as /api/v1/search. Because this endpoint streams results before the ranker finishes, the rank arrives in a separate `sorted_order` SSE event carrying `ordered_domains` (a list of result domains in ranker-preferred order) — apply it client-side to reorder the rows you've buffered.
intent.title: Intent

description.description: All semantic exclusions — every concept a company must NOT match. Use this whenever the query says "exclude / not / without / no / except …", and pack multiple exclusions into one string, e.g. "logistics providers, distributors, drinks-only manufacturers". Do NOT phrase exclusions as negatives inside the positive `description`; there they are treated as positive signal and hurt precision.
description.title: Description

is_public.description: true = publicly listed companies only; false = private or unknown listing status (coarse — combine with other filters); omit for no filter.
is_public.title: Is Public

StructuredJobs.description:
Where and for what a company is currently HIRING.

Read from a weekly scrape of company job boards, active postings only. Two
things callers get wrong:

* This is not the company's headquarters. A US-headquartered company hiring
  in Bengaluru matches `jobs.countries=["India"]` and
  `location.countries=["United States"]` at the same time, and both are true.
* Combining axes matches ONE POSTING where the search can be answered from
  Postgres alone: `cities=["Austin"]` with `departments=["Engineering"]` then
  means an engineering posting in Austin. A search that also carries a
  `description` is answered through the retriever's index, which holds
  per-company arrays and cannot express "the same posting", so that shape
  can return a company with an Austin posting and a separate engineering
  posting.

Within one axis the values are contains-ANY. Coverage is partial: about 20k
companies have any posting data at all, so any job filter narrows hard.
StructuredJobs.title: StructuredJobs

description.description: Free-text semantic concept describing what the company SHOULD be (the only fuzzy field; matched by an LLM verifier). Describe only the positive concept — do NOT embed exclusions or negations here ("exclude X", "not Y", "without Z"); put those in `filters.exclude.description`, or they are read as positive signal and pull in the companies you meant to exclude.
description.title: Description

cursor.description: Opaque pagination token from a previous response's `next_cursor`. When set, resumes the same paged session (server-side filters/description are pinned to the first call) instead of starting a new search.
cursor.title: Cursor
